brief.recommendation: Waiting costs ~$133,624 in lost checkout revenue (596s remaining at $13,452/min loss rate) and EXCEEDS the 60s degradation tolerance. Terminating costs only a 2-minute replay of the idempotent price_sync job (replayable=True, policy=may_interrupt). No protected settlements in flight (DB-2) and no change-calendar window blocks interruption (BIZ-3). Workload registry confirms batch_replayable_price_sync is BATCH_REPLAYABLE with replay cost 2 min (BIZ-2).

audit.report: A batch price-sync job (pid 105041) held an idle-in-transaction lock for 4 seconds, blocking checkout sessions and degrading success to 55% with $4,155/min revenue at risk. The Database Guardian initially proposed waiting, but trade-off analysis showed the job had ~596s remaining, projecting $133,624 in lost checkout revenue—far exceeding the 60s degradation tolerance. Both guardians agreed to terminate the replayable, idempotent job (2-minute replay cost, policy may_interrupt). Termination executed in 67s, but verification failed: a new blocker (pid 105273, same job type) appeared with checkout still at 29% success, so the incident was escalated.
audit.root_cause: An idle-in-transaction batch_replayable_price_sync job blocked checkout sessions, and termination of the first instance did not prevent a second instance from immediately acquiring the same lock pattern.
lessons: For batch_replayable_price_sync: add a pre-run lock-timeout (e.g., SET lock_timeout = '5s') so idle-in-transaction holders self-abort before blocking checkout.
For batch_replayable_price_sync: configure the scheduler to serialize runs or add a singleton advisory lock so only one instance can hold the catalog lock at a time.
For batch_replayable_price_sync: extend the verifier's verification window to 30s and require zero idle-in-transaction batch_worker sessions before marking recovery verified.
audit.negotiation_critique: The Database Guardian correctly pivoted from wait to terminate after the trade-off calculator quantified the cost of waiting ($133k) versus terminating (2-min replay); the Continuity Guardian accepted without objection. No rounds were wasted, but neither guardian anticipated that the scheduler would immediately restart a new instance that replicated the same lock contention.
follow_ups: Add lock_timeout and advisory-lock serialization to the batch_replayable_price_sync job definition and redeploy.
Update the recovery playbook for this workload to include 'verify no new batch_worker idle-in-txn sessions' as a verification gate.
Alert on-call when checkout success drops below 90% for >15s to catch lock contention earlier.

events.title: R1 proposes wait

proposal.rationale: The root blocker (pid 105041, batch_replayable_price_sync) has been idle in transaction for only 4.0s (DB-1). Checkout is degraded at 55% success (TEL-1) and 77% over 10s (BIZ-1), with $4,155/min revenue at risk. However, the business tolerates up to 60s of degraded checkout (BIZ-1). Since the blocker's transaction is very recent (4s) and may complete shortly, waiting avoids the risk of terminating a batch worker that could be mid-critical-section. Memory shows terminating a similar batch_replayable_inventory job restored checkout (MEM-1), but that was a different workload (inventory_reconcile vs price_sync) and the blocker there may have been stuck longer. We lack workload registry, change calendar, protected settlements, and tradeoff data to assess interrupt cost vs wait cost.
proposal.expected_effect: If the blocker commits/rolls back within the next ~56s (within the 60s tolerance), locks release and checkout recovers without intervention. If it persists beyond ~50s, we will need to escalate or terminate in a subsequent round.
proposal.risk_assessment: If the blocker is stuck (e.g., waiting on external resource, deadlock not detected, or application bug), checkout remains degraded beyond 60s, breaching business tolerance and risking ~$4,155/min. Terminating blindly could leave price sync in inconsistent state if not idempotent/replayable.
